name: Dedicated small-launch price per kg
question: Q1
rationale: 12 M EUR for 700 kg is about 19000 USD/kg; Electron earns about 28000 USD/kg

name: Payload fill rate per launch
question: Q1
rationale: No public data; a single 200 kg customer fills only about 30% of a launch

name: Price per Spectrum launch
question: Q1
rationale: Not published; estimates 10–15 M EUR; NewSpace Index about 10 M USD; Electron earns 8.5 M USD for a third of the capacity

name: Rideshare price per kg
question: Q1
rationale: SpaceX list price 2027; about 10000 USD/kg with separation system

name: US government demand open to Isar
question: Q1
rationale: NSPM-17 sends US government payloads to US-built launchers

name: Other governments' demand open to Isar
question: Q1
rationale: Japan, India, Korea and others mostly fly their own launchers

name: Launch sites
question: Q1
rationale: 0 = Andøya only (Q1 today); 1 = plus Nova Scotia (45–98° from 2028); 2 = plus Kourou (low inclinations and GTO)

name: Spectrum launches per year
question: Q1
rationale: Isar's plan for 2027 as its first full operating year; one launch in 2026; production is the bottleneck

name: Share of the serviceable market that buys a dedicated launch
question: Q1
rationale: Measured 2025: 6.7% of SAM satellites (4.2% of mass) flew on a small launcher, all on Rocket Lab's Electron; the rest rode SpaceX rideshare. BryceTech: 10–14% in the West. Planet: new rockets get demo payloads first

name: Launch success rate
question: Q1
rationale: Insurance of about 25% on Isar's next mission implies 75%; mature launchers reach 92–95%

name: Base year of flown demand
question: Q1
rationale: Latest full year; 2024 as comparison shows how much a single year swings

name: Market growth outside megaconstellations
question: Q2+
rationale: Novaspace forecast implies about 9% a year; BryceTech history 13–17%
